outcomes.text: Study Catholic beliefs, practices, sources of authority and forms of expression within Christianity as a whole.
Explore Catholic ideas of God as creator, humans as the image of God, and stewardship.
Explain the meaning of Michelangelo's Creation of Adam and how it shows Catholic beliefs about God as creator.
Contrast it with one other Christian artistic expression of creation.
Explain what Genesis 1 and 2 show about God as creator, transcendent and omnipotent.
Explain the belief that humans are made in God's image and its effect on free will, stewardship, dignity and sanctity of life.
Describe the Bible's origin, structure and literary forms, and Catholic views of inspiration and revelation.
Explain different Christian understandings of the Genesis creation accounts.
Explain natural law and how it shapes views on the sanctity of life.
Explain the Second Vatican Council's view of harmony between science and religion.
Explain care for the environment as loving our neighbour.
Describe how Catholics can carry out stewardship locally, nationally and globally.
Explain the significance of CAFOD's work on sustainability.
Explore the incarnation as God revealed in human form, and Jesus' teaching as moral authority.

subtopics.title: Forms of expression - symbol and incarnation

outcomes.text: Explain the Christian symbols Ichthus, Alpha and Omega, and Chi-Rho.
Explain how belief in the incarnation influences Catholic views of religious art.
Explain the meaning of one statue of Jesus and different Christian views on images of Jesus.
Explain the scriptural origins of Jesus as incarnate Son and divine Word.
Explain Jesus as fully human and fully God, including Son of Man and Son of God.
Explain Jesus as fulfilment of the law and moral teacher, through the Beatitudes and Matthew 25.
Explain Irenaeus' phrase that the glory of God is a human being fully alive.
Compare the incarnation in Dei Verbum 4 and Verbum Domini 12.
Explain grace and the sacramental nature of reality and how incarnation leads to them.
Name the seven sacraments and their effect on sanctifying life.
Explain how imago dei shapes Catholic protection of the unborn.

topics.title: 3.1.3 The Triune God, mission and prayer

outcomes.text: Explore the Trinity, the glory of God, mission and prayer.

subtopics.title: Forms of expression - music and the glory of God

outcomes.text: Describe styles of worship music, including psalms, plainchant, hymns and contemporary songs.
Explain the significance of Mass settings and Eucharistic acclamations.

subtopics.title: Beliefs and teachings on the Trinity

outcomes.text: Explain God as Trinity as expressed in the Nicene Creed, with its scriptural origins.
Explain how Trinity belief influences readings of Genesis 1:1-3.
Explain the influence of the Trinity on Catholic life, mission and evangelism.

subtopics.title: Sources of authority on the Trinity

outcomes.text: Explain the Trinity using Mark 1:9-11 and Galatians 4:6-7.
Compare St Augustine and LaCugna on the intimacy of God's love.
Explain conciliar authority and the Councils of Nicaea and Constantinople.
Explain Baptism as initiation into the life of God.
Explain prayer as raising the heart and mind to God, contrasting traditional and spontaneous prayer.
Explain how prayer and posture are linked in worship.
Explore the Paschal mystery, the Church as Body of Christ and the Eucharist.

subtopics.title: Forms of expression - architecture and design

outcomes.text: Explain how church architecture and decoration reflect Catholic beliefs and aid worship.
Explain how the lectern, altar, crucifix and tabernacle express redemption.
Compare contrasting church artefacts such as altar, plain cross, crucifix and risen Christ.
Explain the death, resurrection and ascension as restoration through sacrifice, recreation and cosmic order.
Compare Christian views on salvation and grace, and the influence of redemption on liturgy.
Identify redemption themes in Mark 15, John 20 and Acts 1 and 2.
Compare salvation metaphors in Irenaeus and Anselm.
Explain conscience as the voice of God and differing Christian views of it.
Explain the Mass as source and summit of Christian life and Eucharist views across denominations.
Link the Words of Institution, Agnus Dei, real presence and sacrifice of the Mass, and Eucharistic adoration.

topics.title: 3.1.5 Church and the Kingdom of God

outcomes.text: Explore the Church's nature, mission and the Kingdom of God.

subtopics.title: Forms of expression - drama and the faith journey

outcomes.text: Explain how dramatised prayer such as the Stations of the Cross reflects the Church as a people on a journey.
Explain the significance of pilgrimage to Jerusalem, Rome, Walsingham and Lourdes.
Explain how mission and evangelism are expressed in drama.

subtopics.title: Beliefs and teachings on the Kingdom

outcomes.text: Explain the Kingdom of God in the Lord's Prayer.
Explain Catholic teaching on justice, peace and reconciliation as signs of the Kingdom.
Explain Church hierarchy and the Second Vatican Council, its history and four key documents.

subtopics.title: Sources of authority on the Church

outcomes.text: Explain Mary as a model of discipleship and the Magnificat.
Explain the four marks of the Church and apostolic succession.
Explain conciliar and pontifical magisterium and Catholic social teaching.

subtopics.title: Practices - Church as Body of Christ

outcomes.text: Explain how Catholic agencies, local and national or global, love neighbours in practice.
Explain how Kingdom values shape vocation through priesthood, family, religious life or community.
Explain how one Catholic figure expressed justice, peace and reconciliation.

topics.title: 3.1.6 Eschatology: Christian life, death and eternity

outcomes.text: Explore Catholic beliefs about life after death and their effect on life today.

subtopics.title: Forms of expression - artefact and eschatology

outcomes.text: Describe the Paschal candle and its significance as an artefact of Resurrection.
Explain the themes of Michelangelo's The Last Judgement.
Explain how beliefs about life after death show in memorials.

subtopics.title: Beliefs and teachings on life after death

outcomes.text: Explain Catholic beliefs about life after death and resurrection, with 1 Corinthians 15.
Explain the four last things: death, judgement, heaven and hell.
Explain purgatory and the difference between particular and final judgement.
Compare Christian beliefs about life after death.
Explain the parable of the Rich Man and Lazarus.
Explain cosmic reconciliation in Julian of Norwich.
Explain Vatican II on eschatology, with Lumen Gentium 48 and Catechism 1037.

subtopics.title: Practices - liturgies of life and death

outcomes.text: Explain the last rites as reconciliation, healing and hope.
Evaluate how the funeral rite reflects beliefs about life after death.
Evaluate how the sanctity of life shapes views on care of the dying and euthanasia.
Study one faith (Islam or Judaism) and two themes, or both textual studies themes.
Study the beliefs, teachings and practices of either Islam or Judaism.
Explain monotheism and God as Creator as teachings common to Christianity and Islam.
Explain different Christian and Muslim understandings of Jesus as prophet and Son of God.
Compare the six articles of faith in Sunni Islam with the five roots of Usul ad-Din in Shi'a Islam.
Explain Tawhid, and God's nature: omnipotence, mercy, justice, immanence and transcendence.
Explain angels, predestination and human freedom.
Explain life after death, accountability, resurrection, heaven and hell.
Explain prophethood and the roles of Adam, Ibrahim and Muhammad.
Explain the authority of the Qur'an and the earlier holy books.
Explain the imamate in Shi'a Islam.
Compare the Five Pillars of Sunni Islam and the Ten Obligatory Acts of Shi'a Islam, including jihad.
Explain the Shahadah and its place in Muslim practice.
Explain how and why Muslims pray, including wudu, rak'ahs, Friday prayer and Sunni and Shi'a differences.
Explain Sawm and the Night of Power during Ramadan.
Explain Zakah and Khums.
Explain Hajj and the actions at Makkah, Mina, Arafat and Muzdalifah.
Explain greater and lesser jihad and the conditions for lesser jihad.
Explain Id-ul-Adha, Id-ul-Fitr and Ashura for Muslims in Britain today.
Explain monotheism and God as Creator as teachings common to Christianity and Judaism.
Explain different Jewish and Christian beliefs about the Messiah.
Explain God as one, Creator, Law-Giver and Judge, loving and merciful.
Explain the divine presence (Shekhinah) and beliefs about life after death.
Explain the Messiah and different views on its role.
Explain the Covenant with Abraham and the promised land.
Explain the Covenant at Sinai, Moses and the Ten Commandments.
Explain key moral principles, Pikuach Nefesh, free will and the 613 mitzvot, and different views on their importance.
Describe the synagogue, its features (bimah, aron hakodesh, ner tamid) and Orthodox and Reform differences.
Explain synagogue services, the Amidah, Shabbat and worship in the home.
Explain the Tenakh and Talmud and their use in daily life.
Explain Brit Milah, Bar and Bat Mitzvah, marriage and mourning rituals.
Explain dietary laws (kosher, trefah, separating milk and meat) and different Jewish views.
Explain Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur and Pesach for Jews in Britain today.
Study two religious, philosophical and ethical themes (A-C) or both textual studies themes (D-E).

subtopics.title: Theme A: Relationships, love and sexuality

outcomes.text: Explain Catholic teaching on sexual love as marital, unitive and procreative, and the Theology of the Body.
Compare Christian and non-religious views on sex before marriage, adultery and same-sex relationships.
Explain the conditions for a valid Catholic marriage, the vows, annulment, divorce and remarrying.
Compare Christian and non-religious views on cohabitation, divorce and same-sex marriage.

subtopics.title: Theme A: Families and gender equality

outcomes.text: Explain Catholic views on family planning, the purpose of the family and roles within it.
Compare Christian and non-religious views on contraception and rights of same-sex parents and single people.
Explain Catholic teaching on the equality of women and men and opposition to gender discrimination.

subtopics.title: Theme B: Violence, justice and forgiveness

outcomes.text: Explain biblical views of violence, forgiveness, reconciliation and justice.
Compare Christian and non-religious views on anger and violent protest.
Explain Just War theory, Catholic views on nuclear weapons and consequences of modern warfare.
Explain religion as a reason for war, Holy War, and Old Testament views on war.
Compare Christian and non-religious views on pacifism and nuclear deterrence.
Explain Catholic views on terrorism, torture, radicalisation and martyrdom.
Explain Christian conflict resolution and peacemaking, with two organisations and examples of nonviolent resistance.

subtopics.title: Theme C: Human rights and wealth

outcomes.text: Explain human dignity, loving your neighbour, human rights and religious freedom.
Explain the link between rights and responsibilities.
Explain Catholic teaching on wealth, stewardship, exploitation and the wealth of the Church.
Compare Christian and non-religious views on greed and materialism.
Explain the Christian duty against poverty, the preferential option for the poor, and the work of CAFOD or Christian Aid.
Compare Christian and non-religious views on responsibility for helping those in poverty.
Explain Christian teaching against racial prejudice and discrimination, equality and justice.
Explain Christian attitudes to prejudice within religion regarding gender and sexuality, and how Christianity promotes tolerance.

subtopics.title: Theme D: Early ministry of Jesus

outcomes.text: Study Mark's early ministry texts: John's preparation, baptism and temptation, the paralysed man, Jairus' daughter, Nazareth and the five thousand.

subtopics.title: Theme D: Later ministry and final days

outcomes.text: Study Mark's later ministry: Caesarea Philippi, transfiguration, passion prediction, James and John, Bartimaeus and the entry into Jerusalem.
Study Mark's final days: Last Supper, Gethsemane, trials, crucifixion and the empty tomb.

subtopics.title: Theme D: Significance of Mark's Gospel

outcomes.text: Explain the titles Son of Man, Son of God, Christ and Son of David for first-century Jews and Christians today.
Explain Mark's portrayal of Jesus as teacher and miracle worker, and Christian and non-religious views on the miracles.
Explain differing beliefs about the Last Supper, Jesus' death and resurrection, and the empty tomb.
Explain differing views on the authority of Mark's Gospel against secular authority.

subtopics.title: Theme E: The Kingdom of God

outcomes.text: Study the parables of the sower, growing seed and mustard seed, Jesus and the children, the rich man and the greatest commandment.

subtopics.title: Theme E: Those disregarded by society

outcomes.text: Study the man with leprosy, call of Levi, Syro-Phoenician woman's daughter, the epileptic boy, the widow's offering and the anointing at Bethany.
Study the first disciples, the woman with a haemorrhage, the mission of the Twelve, cost of discipleship, Peter's denials and the commission.

subtopics.title: Theme E: Significance of Mark's Gospel

outcomes.text: Explain different understandings of the Kingdom of God as present, future, inner and communal.
Explain first-century and Jesus' attitudes to those disregarded, and their significance for Christians.
Explain different views on discipleship, faith and the authority of Jesus' teaching against secular authority.
